reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses oxidation in Nb-silicide-based alloys with different elements (Hf, Si, Sn, Ti, Mo, W) and mentions NICE for balancing properties, but provides no specific support for the claimed synergistic Al-Ti-Cr oxide control in the Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 FCC alloy. The key premises about Al, Ti, and Cr interactions and the application of NICE to this system are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Al, Ti, and Cr synergistically control protective oxide formation in the alloy.
Increased Al content favors a dense, protective alumina or mixed Al/Cr oxide layer.
Ti and Cr adjust the nucleation and growth kinetics of the oxide layer.
Systematic compositional adjustments can shift the balance between protective and non-protective oxide without altering the bulk FCC matrix.
The alloy design methodology NICE can decouple individual elemental contributions to oxide formation.
